title: The Volcanic Eye
description:
THE VOLCANIC EYE

When the Earth erupts, the universe opens its eye.

An exploration of creation, destruction and the awakening of consciousness.

Inspired by the immense force of a volcanic eruption, The Volcanic Eye imagines an eye emerging from the depths of the Earth. Layers of molten reds, earthy textures and organic formations evoke the raw energy of nature, where destruction becomes a catalyst for creation.

The eye represents nature’s gaze — perhaps the universe itself becoming conscious, observing its own continuous transformation. It is both a witness and a manifestation of the forces that shape existence.

The work reflects on the delicate paradox of creation and destruction, suggesting that every ending carries the possibility of another beginning.
The universe is not merely something we inhabit, but something that is constantly looking back at us.

title: THE COSMIC WOMB
description:
The Cosmic Womb explores the idea of creation as an interconnected ,continuous process of becoming . It imagines every womb ;maternal, natural and cosmic — as an expression of the same universal source of life.
Red represents blood, origin, evolution and the force that gives life its beginning. Blue evokes water, movement, fluidity and the perpetual flow of existence. Within these currents, countless faces and eyes emerge, dissolve and coexist, embodying the many expressions of consciousness.
The figures are neither entirely individual nor entirely separate. They are fragments of a greater living whole, connected through an invisible continuum of creation.
The work questions the boundaries between the self and the universe, between the individual and the collective, between birth and rebirth.
Perhaps consciousness is not something we possess individually, but something we participate in.
We are born from the same vastness, exist within its movement, and continue to become.

title: Entangled
description:
Entangled

An exploration of intimacy, identity and the interconnectedness of existence.

This artwork brings together the human body and marine forms in an unusual, almost surreal embrace. Tentacle-like structures surround and intertwine with the female figure, creating a visual language of attachment, vulnerability, protection and entanglement.

The multiple eyes, fluid anatomical forms and intricate patterns reflect the complexity of identity and the invisible threads that connect us to one another and to the natural world.

Perhaps being entangled is simply another way of belonging — to ourselves, to others and to the many forms of life that exist around us.

title: Fragments of Her
description:
Fragments of Her

An exploration of identity, memory and the many selves that exist within a woman.

At the centre of this artwork is a woman surrounded by fragmented faces, watchful eyes and intricate patterns. Multiple figures emerge and disappear within her form, creating a layered visual narrative of selfhood, memory and consciousness.

Each face represents a fragment of being — a thought, an emotion, a memory or an identity shaped by experience. Together, they form an intricate portrait of womanhood, neither singular nor complete, but constantly evolving.

The work reflects on the complexity of being human and the different versions of ourselves that coexist within us.

Perhaps we are all made of fragments, forever becoming.

title: The Collective Unconscious
description:
The Collective Unconscious

What connects us beneath everything that separates us?

A gathering of human figures occupies a shared space, stripped of individual identities and distinguishing features. Their bodies come together beneath a vast circular form, suggesting a common origin, a shared memory or an invisible force that binds humanity.

Inspired by the idea of the collective unconscious, this work explores the deeper layers of human existence — the instincts, fears, memories and experiences that transcend individual identity.

In today’s world, where we are constantly defined by our identities, beliefs, nationalities, ideologies and differences, the artwork reflects on what remains when these labels fall away. The figures are neither representations of a particular gender nor individuals belonging to a specific community. They are simply human.

The intense red landscape evokes the turbulence of our contemporary world — its conflicts, contradictions, collective anxieties and restless transformations. Against this backdrop, the figures exist together, suggesting both the fragility and interconnectedness of human life.

Perhaps beneath everything we have been taught to become, there is something fundamentally shared.

Before identity, before division, before we had names — there was simply us.

title: What Holds Us
description:
What Holds Us

An exploration of human connection, intimacy and the invisible structures that bind us together.

Intertwined bodies, overlapping faces and embracing gestures form a composition that speaks of our innate need for connection. The figures appear almost inseparable, their forms merging into one another through touch, proximity and shared presence.

The branching patterns across their bodies evoke the intricate networks of life, suggesting that beneath our individual identities, we are connected in ways we may never fully understand.

Set against a rigid, geometric backdrop, the figures represent a more instinctive world of human emotion — one that seeks warmth, belonging and reassurance.

Perhaps what holds us together is not always visible. Sometimes it is simply the presence of another.

title: The Unseen Morning
description:
An entire universe exists within a single human being.

A gathering of selves, fragmented thoughts, memories, contradictions and emotions, occupying the same inner space. Some remain visible, others dissolve into the background, yet each belongs to the same consciousness.

Beyond the enclosing wall, a bright morning unfolds. The outside world carries on, unaware of the many worlds existing within.

The painting explores the quiet contrast between inner complexity and outer stillness — the unseen landscapes we inhabit while appearing to simply exist.

Perhaps every person carries a morning that the world will never witness.

title: LACUNA
description:
LACUNA explores the paradox of freedom, desire and self-dissolution. Inspired by the image of a moth drawn towards the very fire that threatens its wings, the work inhabits the fragile territory between liberation and destruction.

An intricate, almost mythical anatomy emerges, where the boundaries between human, animal and the unknown become indistinguishable. A body that holds multiple possibilities of existence, caught somewhere between creation and disappearance.

The work questions whether freedom is always an act of becoming, or sometimes an invitation to unmake oneself.

Perhaps what we seek to escape is also what gives us form.

title: Beyond
description:
Beyond

Beyond the boundaries of religion, identity and inherited beliefs lies a personal understanding of existence.
This artwork is an expression of my inner world, where motherhood, mythology, nature and the idea of the infinite come together. At its centre is Maa Kali, surrounded by animal forms, multiple eyes and intricate organic patterns. The imagery reflects my fascination with the many expressions of the universe and the mysterious ways in which we experience the unknown.

I don’t wish to confine the infinite to a name or a religion. I only know that I found an immense light in you, Kaali — a light I call Allah.

Born from a deeply personal space of contemplation, this work explores the coexistence of different cultural and spiritual influences without seeking to define or reconcile them.

Beyond is an exploration of existence, motherhood, humanity and the infinite light within — something that perhaps cannot be explained, only felt.

title: Kali and Her Many Forms
description:
Kali and Her Many Forms

An exploration of the feminine as an expression of nature, creation and transformation.
This artwork brings together the image of a woman and the organic language of flowers, leaves, intricate patterns and natural forms. Her presence seems to emerge from the very elements that surround her, blurring the boundaries between the human, the natural and the divine.

Inspired by the symbolism of Maa Kali and the multifaceted nature of womanhood, this piece reflects on feminine energy beyond conventional representations. She is both delicate and powerful, rooted and ever-changing, an embodiment of creation in its many forms.
Perhaps the woman and the goddess are not separate, but different expressions of the same infinite existence.

title: The Unfinished Species — Between Births
description:
THE UNFINISHED SPECIES — Between Births

An exploration of humanity as an unfinished journey. Moving through cycles of birth, death, suffering, resistance and renewal, we remain in a constant state of becoming. The cocoon becomes a world within itself — a womb, a refuge and a space of transformation. Rooted in the contradictions of our collective existence, the work questions whether humanity has truly evolved, or is still travelling towards its next beginning.

Perhaps we are not yet born…we are simply between births.

title: Kundalini — The Cosmic Chakra
description: An exploration of human nature as a reflection of the cosmos. Inspired by Kundalini and chakra philosophy, this artwork brings together serpents, human forms and elemental forces to explore the relationship between instinct, consciousness and universal energy. It reflects my fascination with the unseen forces that connect all existence, where the primal and the spiritual coexist, and the human being becomes a universe within itself.
